description: We are students with hopes and dreams, eager to create something innovative, creative, and fun alongside NASA—challenging ourselves and learning more about space and about ourselves.
summary: Space Papers is a browser game for ages 10–12 about making lunar mission decisions. Players review expedition documents at a lunar operations desk, consult a field manual and resource inventory, then approve or return each proposal. Their choices shape mission outcomes and the base’s ability to respond to emergencies and keep operating. The game turns life-support trade-offs into a hands-on learning experience: players compare requested supplies with available food, water, oxygen, propellant and energy, and see the consequences of their decisions. It combines a tactile, animated 2.5D office with short explanations grounded in NASA educational resources. Space Papers helps young players practice evidence-based decisions while distinguishing the game’s fictional balancing rules from real NASA observations.
details:
Space Papers is an interactive lunar operations game created by Los valar for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players work at a lunar operations desk, examining expedition proposals, consulting a field manual and inventory, and stamping each proposal approved or returned. Food, water, oxygen, propellant and energy are limited, so each decision has consequences for missions and the base. Emergencies and base operations introduce further choices about life support, radiation protection, power and food production.

The game makes resource trade-offs tangible through physical documents, stamps, animated characters and a 2.5D office. Reports explain outcomes, while NASA educational references provide context for water recovery, growing food, space weather and communication delays. The game is an educational fiction: its resource costs, probabilities and outcomes are designed for play and are not NASA telemetry or predictions.

Built with TypeScript, HTML and CSS, Vite and Web Audio, the game runs in a browser and its distributed version can be opened offline. The team supplied the 2.5D artwork, including renders from Blender. Keyboard controls, reduced-motion settings and audio controls support different ways to play. OpenAI Codex assisted with code and documentation; this project description was also prepared with its assistance.
